what_it_is.prose: The HAL Tejas Mk-1A is a 4.5-generation single-engine delta-wing multirole light fighter developed by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) as the final integrator, with design by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA). The Mk-1A is an upgrade over the earlier Mk-I, incorporating the indigenous Uttam AESA radar (replacing the Israeli EL/M-2052 used on the initial batch), the indigenous Swayam Raksha Kavach electronic warfare suite, beyond-visual-range Astra Mk-1 air-to-air missiles, and ASRAAM within-visual-range missiles. Private-sector airframe suppliers include L&T (wings), VEM Technologies (centre fuselage), and Alpha Tocol (rear fuselage); Astra Microwave Products supplies Active Antenna Array Units for the Uttam AESA radar under a ₹2,205 crore contract signed 31 July 2026. Indigenous content is 50% on the first aircraft of the 2021 contract, rising to 60% by end of that contract, and 64%+ on the second (97-aircraft) contract signed September 2025. Production capacity is 16 per year at Bengaluru Plants I and II, rising to 24 per year with the Nashik line (operational October 2024), and a planned 32 per year with Nashik II. The Tejas Mk-1A is powered by the GE F404-GE-IN20 engine (USA) — the same engine as the Mk-I. Two major contracts have been signed: the first on 3 February 2021 for 73 Mk-1A and 10 Mk-1 trainers (₹48,000 crore including ₹1,202 crore D&D), and the second on 25 September 2025 for 68 fighters and 29 trainers (97 aircraft total, ₹62,370 crore). HAL also placed a 99-engine contract with GE Aerospace on 17 August 2021 (₹5,375 crore) and a 113-engine contract on 7 November 2025 (₹8,870 crore). On 31 March 2026, HAL announced a third order for 180 Tejas Mk-1A, bringing the total order book for the type to 350 aircraft. The single most critical programme risk is the F404-IN20 engine supply chain: only 6 of 99 engines contracted in August 2021 had been delivered as of April 2026, with the chokepoint traced to a South Korean firm with financial issues. HAL has levied liquidated damages on GE Aerospace and an in-country F404 depot is being established with GE (announced April 2026). First deliveries slipped from February 2024 to March 2026 and remain pending ASQR certification. The Tejas Mk-2 will use the GE F414-INS6 engine, which saw a reported 3x price hike in June 2026.

deployments_procurement.summary: The Tejas Mk-1A programme has three major IAF contracts: (1) 73 Mk-1A + 10 Mk-1 trainers (₹48,000 crore, 3 February 2021); (2) 68 fighters + 29 trainers = 97 aircraft (₹62,370 crore, 25 September 2025); (3) 180 Tejas Mk-1A (₹62,370 crore, March 2026). Total Tejas Mk-1A order book: 350 aircraft. Engine contracts: 99 F404-IN20 (₹5,375 crore, 17 August 2021) + 113 F404-IN20 (₹8,870 crore, 7 November 2025). Astra Microwave received ₹2,205 crore contract on 31 July 2026 for 122 Active Antenna Array Units + 121 Interface Frames for Uttam AESA. First deliveries slipped from February 2024 to March 2026 and remain pending ASQR certification — only 5 of 10 planned FY26 airframes delivered, with 20 airframes ready of the full 180 programme.

faq.question: Why are Tejas Mk-1A deliveries delayed?
faq.answer: First deliveries slipped from February 2024 to March 2026 and remain pending ASQR certification. The critical chokepoint is the GE Aerospace F404-IN20 engine supply chain: only 6 of 99 engines contracted in August 2021 had been delivered as of April 2026, with the chokepoint traced to a South Korean firm with financial issues. HAL has levied liquidated damages on GE Aerospace and an in-country F404 depot is being established with GE (announced April 2026). A separate issue was a charge amplifier that Denmark prohibited from exporting in September 2024 — HAL reassigned this to a Bengaluru firm for indigenous development.

faq.question: What is the indigenous content of the Tejas Mk-1A?
faq.answer: Indigenous content is 50% on the first aircraft of the 2021 contract, rising to 60% by the end of that contract, and 64%+ on the second (97-aircraft) contract signed September 2025 (per HAL). The indigenous content includes the airframe (L&T wings, VEM centre fuselage, Alpha Tocol rear fuselage), the Uttam AESA radar (DRDO-designed, Astra Microwave Active Antenna Array Units), the Swayam Raksha Kavach EW suite, and the Astra Mk-1 BVRAAM. The single largest imported component is the GE F404-IN20 engine.

faq.question: Has the Tejas been exported?
faq.answer: As of August 2026, the HAL Tejas has not been exported, though discussions have been reported with Argentina and Egypt. Argentina has expressed interest in the Tejas Mk-1A as a replacement for its aging fighter fleet, but no contract has been signed. Egypt has also been reported as a potential customer. The Tejas would compete in the light fighter market against the Pakistani-Chinese JF-17 and the Korean FA-50. HAL's FY26 export revenue was ₹501 crore, driven primarily by Do-228 deliveries to Guyana and Mauritius, not Tejas exports.
